results.title: Gongronema latifolium and Ocimum gratissimum impair liver in diabetic rats.
results.content: Original article title: Polyherbal extracts from gongronema latifolium and ocimum gratissimum impaired liver function in alloxan induced diabetic rats. Full text available for: Polyherbal extracts from gongronema latifolium and ocimum gratissimum impaired liver function in alloxan induced diabetic rats. The study investigates the effects of polyherbal extracts from Gongronema latifolium and Ocimum gratissimum on liver function in alloxan-induced diabetic rats. The study demonstrated that co-administration of the extracts resulted in a reduction in blood glucose levels in treated diabetic rats. In conclusion, while the extracts from Gongronema latifolium and Ocimum gratissimum exhibit hypoglycemic properties and potential benefits for diabetes management, their administration may pose risks to liver function, necessitating careful evaluation of their safety and efficacy in therapeutic applications. The study aimed to investigate the effects of co-administering gongronema latifolium and ocimum gratissimum extracts on liver function in alloxan-induced diabetic rats over four weeks. The study suggests that while ocimum gratissimum and gongronema latifolium can lower blood glucose, their co-administration may also lead to harmful effects on liver function at higher doses. In the context of the study, blood analysis, including glucose and liver enzyme levels, was crucial for evaluating the physiological effects of the herbal extracts on diabetic rats, highlighting its importance in diagnosing and monitoring health conditions. This study exemplifies scientific inquiry by investigating the effects of polyherbal extracts on diabetic rats, thereby contributing to the understanding of herbal medicine's potential therapeutic roles and their biochemical impacts on liver function, emphasizing the necessity of empirical validation in modern medicine. The study investigated the effects of herbal extracts on liver function, revealing that these extracts may impair liver health if used excessively. In this study, herbal extracts are investigated as potential drugs in managing diabetes and liver health. The objective of this work was to evaluate one such herbal extract of *Benincasa hispida* fruit for its anti-diabetic activity in experimentally induced diabetic rats. The results of the study at both low and high dose of extract showed significant (p<0.01) decrease in blood glucose levels in diabetic rats. results.content: ## Heliyon. Volume 10, Issue 1, 15 January 2024, e24009. # *In-vivo* anti-hyperglycemic effect of herbal extracts *Tribulus terrestris* (L) and *Curcuma amada* (R) on streptozotocin-induced diabetic rats and its associated histopathological studies. Author links open overlay panel, , , , , , , , ,. Under a Creative Commons license. ## Abstract. Dia/betes is a serious health concern in many countries with high blood glucose, obesity, and multiple organ failures in late stages. Treating diabetes with effective drugs is still a challenging issue since most of the available diabetic drugs are not effective in combating diabetes, especially in secondary disease complications like obesity, retinopathy, and nephropathy associated with diabetes. Hence search for effective antidiabetic medication, especially from natural sources is mandatory with no adverse side effects. In the present study, a combined herbal aqueous extract of *Tribulus terrestris* and *Curcuma amada* was administered to diabetic-induced rats for 37 days. During experimentation, the mean blood glucose level was estimated and at the end of the experiment on the 37th day, the animal was sacrificed and observed for weight gain, plasma insulin, glycogen, glycated hemoglobin, urea, and creatinine level. The results revealed that TT and CA extract-treated diabetic groups significantly lowered the mean blood glucose level followed by increased glycogen and insulin level. Urea, creatinine, and HbA1c levels were considerably reduced in TT and CA-treated diabetic animals as compared to that of antidiabetic drug Glibenclamide-treated groups. TT and CA-treated diabetic animals showed considerable net body weight gain at the end of the experimental day. A concluding remark of the study shows that TT and CA herbal extract is effective against diabetes and it can be considered as an antidiabetic agent in ayurvedic medicine practice. ## Keywords. ## Cited by (0).
